title: Getting a Decision
coreMove: Convert live interest into a defined decision or next step before warmth turns into polite delay.
sourcePressure: Decision chapter: interest and intrigue must become a concrete commitment, because vague enthusiasm is not a decision and needy overexplaining weakens timing.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must avoid generic closing tactics; the chapter is about timing, control, and anti-neediness after the hookpoint has landed.

counterintuition: More explaining can weaken the ask
A next step is not pressure
tryThisNow: Ask for one clear next step
examples: investor says send me your deck

exampleSpecs.domain: clinical trial recruiter pitching a rare-disease site to a hospital research office
exampleSpecs.audience: a recruiter who tends to leave with interest but no enrollment calendar
exampleSpecs.stakes: the study misses its patient window while everyone says the idea is promising
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the director praises the trial, she closes the laptop and asks whether Tuesday or Thursday is the screening-date decision
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a patient-screening calendar on a laptop beside a consent-form packet

exampleSpecs.domain: shipyard automation vendor seeking approval for a welding-cobot pilot
exampleSpecs.audience: a vendor whose demo earns excitement but no pilot owner
exampleSpecs.stakes: the yard delays until the next maintenance shutdown is gone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when supervisors start swapping compliments about the demo, he points to the shutdown calendar and asks who owns the pilot decision by Friday
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a shutdown calendar taped above a steel workbench

exampleSpecs.domain: independent bookstore coalition asking a publisher for regional launch exclusivity
exampleSpecs.audience: a coalition lead who confuses friendly enthusiasm with agreement
exampleSpecs.stakes: the publisher gives polite praise and then routes the launch to national chains
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she marks the exact line where she accepted sounds great instead of asking for the exclusivity decision date
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marked-up launch proposal beside a stack of advance reader copies

exampleSpecs.domain: emergency-management consultant pitching a tabletop drill to a county hospital network
exampleSpecs.audience: a consultant facing administrators who agree in principle but defer calendar decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: flu season arrives with no drill owner or date
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, she sends a thank-you email; after, she holds up the open incident calendar and asks the COO to choose the drill slot in the room
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an incident calendar printed on legal paper beside a red binder clip

exampleSpecs.domain: specialty glass maker pitching museum display cases to a traveling-exhibition producer
exampleSpecs.audience: a maker who overexplains after the producer has already leaned in
exampleSpecs.stakes: the exhibit schedule slips if case specs are not selected this week
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when the producer says this could work, he stops talking, places the case-spec sheet in front of her, and asks for the model selection today
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glass corner sample throwing a pale reflection onto a case-spec sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: community solar developer pitching roof leases to a warehouse owners' association
exampleSpecs.audience: a developer whose room likes the economics but avoids owner-by-owner commitments
exampleSpecs.stakes: interconnection capacity expires before enough roofs sign letters of intent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he lets the savings discussion end, then passes a one-page intent form to the three owners whose roofs meet the load threshold
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a roof-load diagram beside three one-page intent forms

skillTargets: choose a decision ask that fits the moment
analyze overexplaining after interest has peaked
evaluate whether a next step is concrete enough to count

tryThisNowSpec: Write the exact decision your next pitch needs, including who decides, by when, and what concrete object proves it happened.
